Trigger: **daily close below 179.53 on volume > 60M** (i.e., above the ~54M norm). Targets 176.21, then ~174.66 (2×ATR). Invalidation: a reclaim of 183.90 (200 SMA) on rising volume.

### What this table actually says (the trade thesis in one paragraph)
**Revenue grew 2.1% but EPS grew 16.0%.** That 8x gap is *not* demand strength — it is (a) **+291 bps of gross margin** worth ~$3.5B of incremental gross profit, (b) **flat R&D** (−0.2%) meaning essentially all incremental gross profit fell through to operating income, and (c) a **2.5% smaller diluted share count** from the buyback. Decomposing the $4,523M gross-profit increase: roughly $3.48B came from margin rate, only ~$1.04B from volume. **Roughly 77% of the gross profit dollar growth was self-inflicted cost/mix improvement, not unit growth.** A trader long AAPL is long margin mix and capital allocation, not a hardware demand recovery. If mix plateaus, EPS growth compresses toward revenue growth very quickly.

**Key annual insight:** FY2023 was a **revenue-declining year (−2.8%)** that still delivered flat EPS ($6.13 vs $6.11) purely on margin expansion + buyback. That is the template. It is fragile: in FY2023, gross margin expansion (+82 bps) plus a lower tax rate (+148 bps of help) plus the buyback offset a $11B revenue decline — a thin outcome. The **Q1 FY24 acceleration to +16% EPS growth is the first genuine re-acceleration in four quarters**, and it is driven by cost of sales *falling* 3.15% while revenue rose 2.07% — a rare and powerful combination.

**SBC watch item:** SBC rose from $7.9B → $10.8B (+37%) in two years even as revenue was flat-to-down. Q1 FY24 SBC was $2,997M vs $2,905M — +3.2% y/y, decelerating but still above revenue growth. This is a real, non-cash cost that flatters operating cash flow relative to true economics.

## 4. Cash Flow — The Strongest Part of the Story

### Q1 FY2024 vs Q1 FY2023 (three months)

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Operating cash flow** | **39,895** | **34,005** | **+17.32%** |
| Capex (PP&E) | 2,392 | 3,787 | −36.8% |
| **Free cash flow** | **37,503** | **30,218** | **+24.11%** |
| Share repurchases | 20,139 | 19,475 | +3.41% |
| Dividends paid | 3,825 | 3,768 | +1.51% |
| SBC tax withholding (net share settlement) | 2,591 | 2,316 | +11.9% |
| **Total cash returned to shareholders** | **26,555** | **25,559** | **+3.90%** |
| Investing cash flow | **+1,927** | −1,445 | swung positive |
| Financing cash flow | −30,585 | −35,563 | 14.0% less outflow |
| Net change in cash (incl. FX) | **+11,237** | −3,003 | n/m |

### Cash-flow quality metrics (these are the numbers to argue about)

- **Cash conversion (OCF ÷ net income) = 39,895 / 33,916 = 1.18x.** Excellent. Earnings are cash-backed, not accrual-manufactured.
- **FCF margin = 37,503 / 119,575 = 31.4%** of revenue. For context, FY2023 full-year FCF margin was 99,584/383,285 = 26.0%. **Q1 FY24 is a 540 bps step-up.**
- **Capex fell 36.8% y/y to $2,392M** — the single largest contributor to FCF outgrowing OCF (+24.1% FCF vs +17.3% OCF). **Capex cuts are not durable; treat ~$3.0–3.8B/quarter as the normalized run-rate and expect FCF growth to converge toward OCF growth.** Anyone extrapolating +24% FCF growth is mis-modeling.
- **FCF per diluted share ≈ 37,503 / 15,558 ≈ $2.41** in one quarter.
- **Shareholder returns consumed 70.8% of FCF** (26,555 / 37,503), leaving ~$10.9B to build cash. Sustainable.

### Annual cash flow history — the capital-return engine

| ($M) | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow | 104,038 | 122,151 | **110,543** |
| Capex | 11,085 | 10,708 | 10,959 |
| **Free cash flow** | **92,953** | **111,443** | **99,584** |
| Share repurchases | 85,971 | 89,402 | 77,550 |
| Dividends | 14,467 | 14,841 | 15,025 |
| **Buyback + dividends** | **100,438** | **104,243** | **92,575** |
| + SBC tax withholding | 6,556 | 6,223 | 5,431 |
| **Total capital returned** | **106,994** | **110,466** | **98,006** |
| **Total returned ÷ FCF** | **115.1%** | **99.1%** | **98.4%** |
| Financing cash flow | −93,353 | −110,749 | −108,488 |
| Investing cash flow | −14,545 | −22,354 | **+3,705** |

**This is the most important structural fact about AAPL:** for three consecutive years it has returned **98–115% of free cash flow** to shareholders — i.e., it pays out *more than it generates*, funding the excess in FY2021 from the securities portfolio. In FY2023, investing activities turned **net positive (+$3,705M)** — Apple became a *net seller/liquidator* of its marketable securities portfolio rather than a net buyer, for the first time in the three-year window. That is a subtle but real signal: **the offshore cash pile is being harvested, not grown, to fund buybacks.**

**Trajectory concern:** total capital returned fell from $110.5B (FY22) → $98.0B (FY23), a −11.3% cut, tracking the −10.6% decline in FCF. Management is being disciplined — payout is proportional to cash generation, not levered up. Good governance sign, but it means **buyback-driven EPS accretion is mechanically shrinking** unless FCF re-accelerates. Q1 FY24's +24% FCF is the first evidence it might.

---

## 5. Balance Sheet — Deleveraging Into a Net-Cash Fortress
